web_search.description: Search the web; returns the top results as title and snippet pairs. Results can be stale or wrong: report them as what the source says.

unit_convert.description: Convert a quantity between units (cups to grams, Fahrenheit to Celsius, miles to kilometres).

get_weather.description: Current conditions and today's forecast for a place.

todo_add.description: Add an item to the user's to-do list, optionally with a due date.

list_add.description: Add an item to a named list (shopping, packing, ...).

dice_roll.description: Roll dice in standard notation; returns each die and the total.

counter.description: A named tally kept during the session (reps, rows, points): increase, decrease, reset or read it.

record_note.description: Save a short note to the user's notes.

ask_frontier.returns: task_id now; later task_done{answer (200-800 words), confidence, sources?}
ask_frontier.notes: Calls a larger frontier model with the full conversation context. The conversation carries on while it runs; the answer is reported briefly and attributed, and read out in full when the user asks for it.
ask_frontier.description: Ask a much larger, slower and smarter model that sees the whole conversation. Use it for hard questions: real reasoning, planning, expert knowledge, careful maths, weighing options, checking long text, or whenever you are not sure. Don't use it for chit-chat, simple commands or facts you already have. Async: returns a task_id at once; the answer (often long) arrives later as task_done, possibly while someone is talking. Report it in one to three sentences unless the user asks for the whole answer; say it came from the bigger model and keep its caveats.

arg_descriptions.question: the full question with its constraints and what the answer is for
arg_descriptions.context: anything relevant that isn't obvious from the conversation

task_status.returns: list<object{task_id, kind, status: running|done|failed, elapsed_s, eta_s?}>
task_status.description: Status of background tasks (ask_frontier, deep_research, summaries, queries, deploys): running, done or failed, seconds elapsed and an estimate of time left. Use it to answer 'is it done yet?' instead of guessing.

arg_descriptions.task_id: omit to list all background tasks

get_time.description: Current local date, time and weekday, optionally in another time zone. The assistant has no clock of its own.

stopwatch.description: A stopwatch: start, stop, lap, read or reset. For timing talks, planks, speeches.

calculator.description: Evaluate an arithmetic expression exactly. Use it rather than mental maths for anything non-trivial.
